question: The Farakka barrage is situated on ______ river.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ganga**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The **Farakka Barrage** is constructed on the **Ganga River**, one of the most important rivers in **India**. It is situated in the **Murshidabad district** of **West Bengal**.

• The primary purpose of the Farakka Barrage is to **divert water** from the Ganga into the **Bhagirathi-Hooghly River system** to ensure the navigability of the Kolkata Port.

• The barrage was **commissioned in 1975** and is a crucial infrastructure for **water resource management** in the region.

• It spans a length of **2,240 meters**, making it one of the largest barrages in the world.

• The Farakka Barrage also plays a significant role in **irrigation**, **flood control**, and **hydropower generation**, benefiting millions of people in **West Bengal and Bihar**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Significance of the Ganga River:**

• The Ganga is the **longest river in India**, with a total length of approximately **2,525 kilometers**, flowing through **India and Bangladesh**.

• It originates from the **Gangotri Glacier** in the **Indian Himalayas** at **Gaumukh** in **Uttarakhand**.

• The river is revered as **sacred** in **Hinduism** and is a lifeline for millions who depend on it for **agriculture, drinking water, and transportation**.

• **Features and Functions of the Farakka Barrage:**

• The barrage includes **109 gates** to regulate water flow effectively.

• It helps maintain the **navigability of the Bhagirathi-Hooghly River**, which was critical for the **economic viability of Kolkata Port**.

• The barrage also assists in controlling the **siltation problem** in the Hooghly River.

• **Environmental Impact:**

• The construction of the Farakka Barrage has led to **changes in the river ecosystem**, affecting aquatic life and fish migration patterns.

• It has also been associated with **water disputes** between India and Bangladesh, particularly regarding the sharing of Ganga water during the dry season.

• **International Context:**

• The **Ganga Water Treaty** was signed in **1996** between **India and Bangladesh** to address water-sharing issues related to the Farakka Barrage.

• This treaty ensures an **equitable distribution of water** during the lean season (January to May), fostering cooperation between the two nations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Disputes and Challenges:**

• The **India-Bangladesh dispute** over water sharing has been a significant issue, as the downstream flow affects agriculture and livelihoods in Bangladesh.

• During the monsoon, the barrage sometimes causes **flooding**, impacting surrounding areas in **West Bengal** and **Bangladesh**.

• **Technical Features:**

• The barrage is equipped with **sluice gates** to manage water levels and flow effectively.

• It also includes a **feeder canal**, which diverts water from the Ganga to the Bhagirathi-Hooghly River.

• **Developmental Role:**

• The Farakka Barrage has contributed to the economic development of **eastern India**, particularly by supporting **irrigation**, **navigation**, and **agriculture**.

• It also aids in generating **hydropower**, contributing to the energy needs of the region.
